#### 5. Syncs, records, orchestration, inbound webhooks

##### Sync script shape — `packages/runner-sdk/lib/scripts.ts` (`createSync`), `sync.ts` (`NangoSyncBase`)
```ts
const sync = createSync({
    description, endpoints: [{ method: 'GET', path: '/shopify/products' }],
    frequency: 'every hour',            // min 30s, max 31 days
    models: { Product: z.object({ id: z.string(), … }) },
    syncType: 'incremental' | 'full',   // deprecated
    trackDeletes: boolean,              // deprecated → nango.trackDeletesStart/End
    autoStart: true, scopes: [...], metadata: zod, checkpoint: zod (flat string|number|boolean),
    webhookSubscriptions: ['products/update', '*'],
    exec: async (nango) => { … }, onWebhook: async (nango, payload) => { … }
});
```
(Legacy `nango.yaml` v2: `syncs.<name>: {runs, sync_type, track_deletes, auto_start, endpoint, output, input, scopes, webhook-subscriptions, version}` parsed by `packages/nango-yaml/lib/parser.v2.ts` into `ParsedNangoSync`; `packages/types/lib/nangoYaml/index.ts`.)

SDK surface inside `exec` (abstract in `runner-sdk/lib/sync.ts`, implemented in `packages/runner/lib/sdk/sdk.ts`): `batchSave(records, model)`, `batchDelete`, `batchUpdate` (deep merge on server), `getRecordsByIds`, `listRecords(model,{cursor})`, `trackDeletesStart(model)` / `trackDeletesEnd(model) → {deletedKeys}`, `deleteRecordsFromPreviousExecutions` (deprecated), `setMergingStrategy({strategy:'ignore_if_modified_after'|'override'}, model)`, `paginate(config)` (async generator using `provider.proxy.paginate` cursor/link/offset — `runner-sdk/lib/paginate.service.ts`), `get/post/…/proxy` with `retries`/`retryOn`/`retryHeader`, `getMetadata/setMetadata`, `getCheckpoint/setCheckpoint`, `lastSyncDate` (Date of the previous successful job, or undefined on first/full run), `log`, `getConnection`, plus a cross-execution **lock API** (`runner/lib/sdk/locks.ts` → persist `/runner/locks/*`, TTL + owner). Every SDK call starts with `this.throwIfAbortedOrKilled()` (cooperative cancellation).

`batchSave` (`sdk.ts` 561): strips `_nango_metadata`, chunks by `this.batchSize`, `POST /environment/:env/connection/:id/sync/:syncId/job/:jobId/records` on the **persist** service with the current merging strategy; the server returns `nextMerging`, which the SDK adopts (this is how `ignore_if_modified_after` becomes `ignore_if_modified_after_cursor` once a cursor is known). Validation against the zod-derived JSON schema per record (`validateRecords`).

**Incremental vs full** — `packages/jobs/lib/execution/sync.ts` 69–130: `syncType = sync_type === 'incremental' && lastSyncDate ? 'incremental' : 'full'`; the script itself decides what to fetch using `nango.lastSyncDate`; `emptyCache` (from "run full resync and delete records") hard-deletes all records of the models first (`clearRecordsIfNeeded`). Legacy `track_deletes` post-step (358–380): after `exec`, `records.deleteOutdatedRecords({generation: syncJobId})` per model.

##### Records store — `packages/records`
`records` table (`stores/postgres/migrations/20240327151027_create_records_table.ts`):
```sql
CREATE TABLE "records" (
  id uuid NOT NULL, external_id varchar(255) NOT NULL, json jsonb, data_hash varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  connection_id integer NOT NULL, model varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  created_at timestamptz …, updated_at timestamptz …, deleted_at timestamptz, sync_id uuid, sync_job_id integer
) PARTITION BY HASH (connection_id, model)   -- 256 partitions
-- UNIQUE (connection_id, model, external_id); UNIQUE (connection_id, model, id); INDEX (connection_id, model, updated_at, id)
```
Triggers: `records_updated_at` bumps `updated_at` **only when `data_hash` changes**; `records_undelete` resets `created_at/updated_at` when a soft-deleted row comes back. Later: `pruned_at`, `size_bytes`; `records_data` (2026-03, `20260327160200_create_data_table.ts`) moves the JSON blob to a side table so a row is rewritten only when the hash changes ("only write data when hash has changed"); `records_seen` (`20260512000100`, range-partitioned per day) holds `record_ids uuid[]` per `(connection_id, model, generation)`; `records_routing` maps `(connection, model)` → store key (multi-store).

`FormattedRecord` (`lib/types.ts`): `{id, external_id, json, data_hash, connection_id, model, sync_id, sync_job_id, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at}`; returned records carry
```ts
_nango_metadata: { first_seen_at, last_modified_at, last_action: 'ADDED'|'UPDATED'|'DELETED', deleted_at, pruned_at, cursor }
```
`helpers/format.ts`: `id = uuid.v5(connectionId+model+external_id, uuid.v5(connectionId+model, NIL))` (stable across runs), `data_hash = md5(JSON.stringify(record))`, `external_id = String(record.id)` with NUL bytes stripped; `softDelete` mode sets `deleted_at` (from `record.deletedAt` or now). `helpers/uniqueKey.ts` dedupes by `external_id` and reports `nonUniqueKeys`. `helpers/merge.ts` deep-merges for `batchUpdate` (arrays replaced, not concatenated). `cursor.ts`: cursor = `base64("${last_modified_at}||${id}")`, validated with zod on decode.

**Upsert = one SQL statement with a change classification** (`stores/postgres/postgres.ts` `upsert`, line 536): per (connection, model) `pg_advisory_xact_lock` (`acquireAdvisoryLock`), chunks of `BATCH_SIZE`, `WITH incoming AS (VALUES …), classified AS MATERIALIZED (SELECT … LEFT JOIN records r ON external_id …)` computing
```sql
CASE WHEN r.external_id IS NULL THEN 'inserted'
     WHEN r.deleted_at IS NOT NULL AND incoming.deleted_at IS NULL THEN 'undeleted'
     WHEN r.deleted_at IS NULL AND incoming.deleted_at IS NOT NULL THEN 'deleted'
     WHEN incoming.data_hash IS DISTINCT FROM r.data_hash THEN 'changed'
     ELSE 'unchanged' END as status
```
and `should_upsert` (hash differs, deleted flag differs, or the optional `(r.updated_at, r.id) <= (cursor)` guard for `ignore_if_modified_after_cursor`) → `INSERT … ON CONFLICT (connection_id, model, external_id) DO UPDATE` only for those rows → `UpsertSummary {addedKeys, updatedKeys, deletedKeys, unchangedKeys, nonUniqueKeys, activatedKeys (monthly-active accounting), nextMerging}`. Wrapped in `retry()` for deadlocks.

**Delete detection by generation** — `deleteOutdatedRecords({connectionId, model, generation, batchSize=10_000})` (postgres.ts 1373): pages live rows by `id > lastId`, anti-joins against `SELECT unnest(record_ids) FROM records_seen WHERE … AND generation >= :generation` and soft-deletes the rest; each batch is its own transaction under the advisory lock ("deletion is intentionally not atomic … the next sync run will call deleteOutdatedRecords again and clean up whatever was missed"). `trackDeletesStart` saves `{syncJobId}` in a checkpoint keyed by model; `trackDeletesEnd` calls persist `DELETE …/job/:jobId/outdated` with that job id, so everything not seen since the start marker is tombstoned (`deleted_at`, `last_action: DELETED`). Old `sync_job_id` on `records` is deprecated ("records_seen owns the generation").

Delete modes: `deleteRecords({mode: 'hard'|'soft'|'prune'})`; daemons `autopruning` (drop JSON of stale records, keep tombstone) and `autodeleting`.

##### Orchestrator / scheduler / jobs / runner
- **`packages/scheduler`** — two Postgres tables (`20240506105059_initial_scheduler_models.ts`): `tasks(id, name, payload, group_key, group_max_concurrency, retry_max, retry_count, retry_key, owner_key, starts_after, created_to_started_timeout_secs, started_to_completed_timeout_secs, heartbeat_timeout_secs, state ENUM(CREATED,STARTED,SUCCEEDED,FAILED,EXPIRED,CANCELLED), last_state_transition_at, last_heartbeat_at, output, terminated, schedule_id)` and `schedules(name unique, state PAUSED|STARTED|DELETED, starts_at, frequency_ms, payload, group_key, retry_max, timeouts, last_scheduled_task_id/state, next_execution_at)`. **Partial unique index** `tasks_one_active_per_schedule ON tasks(schedule_id) WHERE state IN ('CREATED','STARTED')` (`20260728085028`).
- **Dequeue** (`models/tasks.ts` 392): `pg_try_advisory_xact_lock(hash(groupKeyPattern))` (skip if another worker is dequeuing the same pattern), then one CTE: candidates `WHERE state='CREATED' AND group_key LIKE ? AND starts_after <= now() FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` → running count per group → `ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY group_key ORDER BY created_at)` → `WHERE group_max_concurrency = 0 OR rank + current_running <= group_max_concurrency` → `UPDATE … SET state='STARTED', last_heartbeat_at=now()` → return.
- **Expiry daemon** (`daemons/expiring/expiring.daemon.ts` + `tasks.expiresIfTimeout`): under an advisory lock, CREATED past `starts_after + created_to_started_timeout` or STARTED past `last_heartbeat_at + heartbeat_timeout` → EXPIRED with `{reason}`; schedules' `next_execution_at` advanced. **Scheduling daemon** (`daemons/scheduling/scheduling.ts`): due = `state='STARTED' AND starts_at<=now AND next_execution_at<=now AND last_scheduled_task_state NOT IN (CREATED,STARTED)` `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`.
- **Retry** (`scheduler.ts` `fail`, 456–510): if `retryMax > retryCount` insert a new task `${name}:${retryCount+1}` with the same `retryKey` (clients poll `/retries/:retryKey/output`).
- **Group keys & concurrency** (`packages/shared/lib/clients/orchestrator.ts`): syncs are recurring schedules named `environment:<envId>:sync:<syncId>`, group `sync:environment:<envId>` with `maxConcurrency: 0` (unbounded; an env `SYNC_ENVIRONMENT_MAX_CONCURRENCY` → `recurringGroupMaxConcurrency` exists in `orchestrator/lib/scheduler-config.ts`), `retry: {max: 0}`, timeouts `createdToStarted 1h, startedToCompleted 24h, heartbeat 5min`; actions `action:environment:<env>` (async actions `maxConcurrency: 1` "runs sequentially per environment"); webhooks `webhook:environment:<env>`; functions `function:environment:<env>:connection:<id>:function:<name>` (per-connection group). `ORCHESTRATOR_TASK_CREATED_PER_GROUP_COUNT_MAX` caps queued tasks per group (`task_dropped` events); `BackpressureMonitor` gauges queued-per-group.
- **`packages/jobs`** — `OrchestratorProcessor` (`orchestrator/lib/clients/processor.ts`): a `PQueue({concurrency})` per `groupKeyPattern`, long-polling `dequeue` for `available + concurrency` tasks, handler failure → `client.failed(taskId)`. `jobs/lib/execution/sync.ts` builds `NangoProps` (connection, syncId, syncJobId, lastSyncDate, track_deletes, secretKey for persist, heartbeatTimeoutSecs, runner flags, usage capping status) and calls the runner; on completion writes the sync job result, fires the `sync` webhook per model `{added, updated, deleted}` and, if any records changed, `modifiedAfter`.
- **`packages/runner`** — `exec.ts`: the compiled script is wrapped in `(function(){ var module={exports:{}}; … })()` and run with **`node:vm` `Script` in a sandbox** whose `console` is a no-op Proxy and whose `require` is a whitelist (`url`, `crypto`, `zod`, `soap`, `botbuilder`, `unzipper`, …); the SDK object is injected; an `AbortController` propagates cancel/kill; output capped at 2 MB. `RunnerMonitor` (`monitor.ts`) holds a **sync-conflict key** `function:${env}:${scriptType}:${syncId}` (locally or via persist `PUT /runner/syncConflict`) so the same sync never runs twice concurrently even if the scheduler misfires; heartbeats go to `jobs /tasks/:id/heartbeat`. Runners are per-team processes (`jobs/lib/runner/runner.ts`: `${env}-runner-account-${teamId}` on Fleet/Kubernetes, Render, Lambda or a single "remote" runner) — customer isolation is by process, not by `vm`.
- **`packages/persist`** — the only service that touches the records DB from scripts; authenticated by the environment secret key; routes for records (`POST/PUT/DELETE …/job/:jobId/records`, `/outdated`, `/hard`), cursor, checkpoints, runner locks, sync-conflict, abort, logs.

##### Inbound webhooks — `packages/server/lib/webhook/*`
- Route `/webhook/:environmentUuid/:providerConfigKey` → `webhook.manager.ts routeWebhook`: 204 if no body+headers, 204 if the provider has no `webhook_routing_script` or no handler; handler contract (`types.ts`):
```ts
export type WebhookHandler<T = any> = (internalNango: InternalNango, headers, body: T, rawBody: string, query?)
    => Promise<Result<WebhookResponse>>;
// WebhookResponse = { content, statusCode } | + { connectionIds: string[] } | + { toForward: unknown } | { content: null, statusCode: 204 }
```
37 handlers exist (`index.ts` re-exports; e.g. shopify, hubspot, salesforce, slack, github-app, jira, linear, xero, airtable, google-*, gmail, notion, pagerduty, shipstation). **There is no `stripe-webhook-routing.ts`** on master (404) — Stripe forwarding without routing is **unverified**.
- **Shopify** (`shopify-webhook-routing.ts`, quoted ≤10 lines):
```ts
function validateShopifySignature(secret: string, headerSignature: string, rawBody: string): boolean {
    const calculatedHmac = crypto.createHmac('sha256', secret).update(rawBody, 'utf8').digest('base64');
    return crypto.timingSafeEqual(Buffer.from(calculatedHmac, 'base64'), Buffer.from(headerSignature, 'base64'));
}
…
const webhookSecret = nango.integration.oauth_client_secret || nango.integration.custom?.['webhookSecret'];
…
const response = await nango.executeScriptForWebhooks({ body, webhookTypeValue: topic ?? '', connectionIdentifierValue: subdomain, propName: 'subdomain' });
return Ok({ content: { status: 'success' }, statusCode: 200, connectionIds, toForward: body });
```
Headers read case-insensitively: `x-shopify-hmac-sha256`, `x-shopify-topic`, `x-shopify-shop-domain` (→ subdomain). `InternalNango.executeScriptForWebhooks` (`internal-nango.ts` 117) resolves connections by `connection_config.<propName>` (or `metadata.<x>`, or `connectionId`), then for each sync config whose `webhook_subscriptions` contains the topic (or `*`) dispatches an `onWebhook` execution through the orchestrator (`webhook:environment:<env>` group) or a queue.
- **Forwarding to the customer** (`webhook.manager.ts` 100–190 + `packages/webhooks/lib/forward.ts`): only when the handler returned 200 and the integration has `forward_webhooks`; **fire-and-forget** ("Forward the webhook to the customer asynchronously to avoid provider timeouts"); per matched connection: body `{from: provider, providerConfigKey, type:'forward', payload, connectionId}` to `primary_url` and `secondary_url` (per-connection `webhook_url_override` honoured). `deliver` (`webhooks/lib/utils.ts` 212): stable-stringified body, headers `X-Nango-Signature` (= sha256(secret+payload), flagged "vulnerable to length-extension attacks") **and** `X-Nango-Hmac-Sha256` (HMAC), original provider headers minus `NON_FORWARDABLE_HEADERS`; `retryFlexible` up to `NANGO_WEBHOOK_RETRY_ATTEMPTS` with backoff `min(3000·2^n, 10 min)`; `shouldRetry`: network errors and non-2xx except `4xx` → retry; timeouts `NANGO_WEBHOOK_TIMEOUT_MS`; egress URL policy (`isOutboundUrlAllowed`). **Circuit breaker per destination URL** (`circuitBreaker.ts`, Redis `rate-limiter-flexible` failure counter: `failureThreshold` in `windowSecs` → OPEN for `cooldownDurationSecs` → HALF_OPEN single probe).
- Sync-completion webhook (`webhooks/lib/sync.ts` `sendSync`): `{type:'sync', connectionId, providerConfigKey, syncName, syncVariant, model, responseResults:{added,updated,deleted}, syncType, modifiedAfter, success, error?}`; auth webhooks (`auth.ts`) for creation/refresh/override with success/error.

---

#### 6. Proxy — `packages/server/lib/controllers/proxy/allProxy.ts` + `services/proxy.service.ts` + `packages/shared/lib/services/proxy/*`

Request headers (`allProxy.ts` 105–125): `Connection-Id`, `Provider-Config-Key`, `Retries` (number, default 0), `Retry-On` (comma-separated status codes → `retryOn: number[]`), `Base-Url-Override`, `Decompress`, `Forward-Headers-On-Redirect`, `Nango-Activity-Log-Id`, `Nango-Is-Sync`, `Nango-Is-Dry-Run`, and any `Nango-Proxy-<Header>` is forwarded as `<Header>`. Endpoint = everything after `/proxy/` including the query string.

`proxy.service.ts request` (216–345): load connection → `refreshOrTestCredentials({instantRefresh:false})` **before the first attempt**; build `ApplicationConstructedProxyConfiguration` via `getProxyConfiguration` (`proxy/utils.ts` 210: strips the base_url if the caller passed an absolute URL, `retries || 0`, `retryOn`, `decompress`, files); then `new ProxyRequest({ proxyConfig, getConnection, getIntegrationConfig, outboundPolicy, logger })`. **`getConnection` is invoked on every attempt** (memoised for `MEMOIZED_CONNECTION_TTL`) and re-runs `refreshOrTestCredentials`, which is why a `401` is in the default retryable set ("Maybe: token was refreshed").

`ProxyRequest.request` (`proxy/request.ts` 100–200): `retryFlexible(fn, { max: retries, onError })` — `fn` rebuilds the axios config each attempt (`getAxiosConfiguration`: URL, headers, agents with SSRF policy, byte-metering transport, redirect validation). `retryFlexible` (`packages/utils/lib/retry.ts`): attempt loop, `nextWait = min(3000·2^attempt, 600000)`, `onError` may return `{retry, reason, wait}` and the custom `wait` wins.

**Retry decision** (`proxy/retry.ts` `getProxyRetryFromErr`): network error codes (`ECONNRESET, ETIMEDOUT, ECONNABORTED, ECONNREFUSED, EHOSTUNREACH, EAI_AGAIN, UND_ERR_SOCKET` + env extras) → retry; if the provider declares `proxy.retry.error_code` (exact `429`, class `5xx`, range `500-502`) only those; else default `status >= 500 || 429 || 401`; then caller `retryOn`; then `remaining` header `=== '0'`. Wait time precedence: caller `retryHeader {at|after}` → provider `proxy.retry.at|after` (list; **longest** wait across headers wins) → `in_body {path, value regex, strategy}` → exponential backoff. `parseRetryValue`: `at` accepts epoch seconds, epoch ms (year > 1971 heuristic) or a date string, wait = `reset - now`; `after` = seconds (their TODO: "handle non-seconds header (e.g: linear)").

**URL building** (`proxy/utils.ts buildProxyURL` 419): `apiBase = baseUrlOverride || provider.proxy.base_url`; the `A || B` fallback is resolved by finding the first `connectionConfig.<key>` in the template and picking `A` if that key is set, else `B`; the endpoint is stripped of the base only at a real path boundary (anti `api.example.com.evil.com`); then `interpolateIfNeeded` with `{...connection (connection_config, metadata), ...credentials}`; `provider.proxy.query` interpolated with `{accessToken, connectionConfig, credentials, ...credentials}`. Headers: `provider.proxy.headers` interpolated the same way (`${accessToken}` = OAuth2 `access_token` or `.token`; `${clientId}/${clientSecret}` need the integration config). `Base-Url-Override` is subject to `enforceProxyOutboundUrlPolicy` + a denylist (`packages/egress`, `runner-sdk/lib/baseUrlOverrideDenylist.ts`) — private/metadata IPs are blocked.

Per-provider pagination in the SDK (`nango.paginate`) is driven by `provider.proxy.paginate` (cursor: `cursor_path_in_response`/`cursor_name_in_request`; link: `link_rel_in_response_header`/`link_path_in_response_body`; offset: `offset_name_in_request`, `offset_calculation_method`).

---

#### 7. Rate limiting and concurrency

- **Public API** (`packages/server/lib/middleware/ratelimit.middleware.ts`): `rate-limiter-flexible` (Redis, memory fallback), fixed 60-s window, key `account-secret-<id>` / `account-global-<id>` (+`-script` bucket when `Nango-Is-Script: true`), `user-<id>`, or `ip-<ip>`; plan size `s…12xl` = multiples of `DEFAULT_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MIN`; sensitive paths cost `max/6` points, unauthenticated calls cost 10; responds `X-RateLimit-Limit/Remaining/Reset`, `429 {error:{code:'too_many_request'}}` + `Retry-After`; **fails open** if Redis is down (docs: `docs/reference/backend/http-api/rate-limits.mdx`).
- **Webhook ingress** (`webhook-ingress-ratelimit.middleware.ts`): key `${environmentUuid}:${providerConfigKey}`, `enforce` flag, same headers.
- **Orchestrator immediate-task throttle** (`orchestrator/lib/rateLimiter.ts` + `kvstore/lib/SlidingWindowRateLimiter.ts`): Lua sliding window (previous window weighted by remaining fraction), `ORCHESTRATOR_THROTTLED_IMMEDIATE_PER_MIN`, returns `retryAfterMs`.
- **Outbound to providers**: **no per-connection or per-provider outbound rate limiter.** Only reactive handling: `retries` + header-driven waits (§6). Docs (`docs/guides/functions/rate-limits.mdx`) explicitly say "Strategy 1: retry with exponential backoff … sync functions can run for up to 24 hours".
- **Concurrency control per connection**: (a) Redis refresh lock per connection (§3); (b) `records` advisory lock per (connection, model) for upsert/delete; (c) one active task per schedule (partial unique index) + runner sync-conflict key per `(env, scriptType, syncId)`; (d) task group `group_max_concurrency` — `action` async 1 per environment, functions grouped per connection, syncs unbounded per environment by default; (e) `updateLastFetched` uses `SKIP LOCKED` to avoid lock convoys. A sync of one connection and an action on the same connection **can** run concurrently.

---

#### 8. What Nango gets wrong / what is over-engineered for a single-tenant PIM

**Over-engineered for us (multi-tenant SaaS control plane):**
- Accounts → environments → plans → usage/metering/capping (`packages/billing`, `metering`, `usage`; `capping.getStatus(...)` is called on the hot path of sync, webhook and proxy), connect sessions / end users / keystore, Slack notifications, audit trails, ClickHouse/ElasticSearch logs, `dd-trace` on every function.
- Five services talking HTTP (server, orchestrator, jobs, persist, runner) plus Redis pub/sub just so a popup can be notified by whichever instance holds the socket; fleet/Kubernetes/Render/Lambda runner provisioning per customer; `node:vm` sandbox + compiled-script upload to S3 + the whole `nango.yaml`/zod → JSON-schema compile & deploy pipeline (`packages/nango-yaml`, `shared/lib/services/deploy`). For one tenant, a sync is a function in our own process.
- Records: 256 hash partitions + `records_data` side table + daily-partitioned `records_seen` + auto-pruning/deleting daemons + MAR accounting (`activatedKeys`) — sized for hundreds of millions of rows across tenants.
- 982-provider catalogue with 17 auth modes (MCP OAuth, TBA, BILL, TWO_STEP with SAML assertions…) — we need ≈10 commerce providers and 3 modes.
- Per-record encryption option and KMS envelope keys.

**Actually wrong or weak (worth avoiding, not copying):**
- Refresh lock is admittedly "not a distributed lock" (single Redis, unsafe on crash); combined with the in-process promise map it is good enough only because refreshes are idempotent-ish. No fencing token.
- `refresh_attempts` is incremented **per calendar day**, so a connection broken on Friday night is only `refresh_exhausted` on the 4th day; meanwhile every sync retries. Fine for them (they bill), noisy for us.
- No `refresh_token_expires_at`: eBay (18 months), Amazon LWA and Etsy refresh-token lifetimes are invisible until failure. `credentials_expires_at` defaults to `now+1 day` for tokens without expiry, which makes the column meaningless for BigCommerce/Shopify offline tokens.
- OAuth `state` cookie is measured but not enforced (feature flag); HMAC verification uses `===`; the popup posts to `window.opener` with `'*'` origin.
- `X-Nango-Signature` (sha256(secret+payload)) is kept for backward compatibility despite their own "vulnerable to length-extension" comment.
- `at:` retry headers assume seconds ("TODO: handle non-seconds header"); `after:` assumes seconds; `in_body` regex config in YAML is fragile.
- `A || B` base-url fallback is parsed with a regex on the first `connectionConfig.<key>` — an implicit, undocumented rule.
- `data_hash = md5(JSON.stringify(record))` is key-order sensitive (a script that emits the same object with different key order will "update" every record). They do stable-stringify webhook bodies but not records.
- The commerce entries carry **no** rate-limit metadata (Shopify leaky bucket / `X-Shopify-Shop-Api-Call-Limit`, SP-API token bucket, eBay daily quotas), so the proxy's clever header logic is unused for exactly the APIs we care about.
- `sync:environment:<env>` groups run unbounded; per-connection fairness is not modelled (one big connection can starve the rest).
- Webhook forwarding is fire-and-forget after the provider gets its 200 — a crash between the two loses the event (no outbox).

---

| # | Pattern | Why | Nango file that demonstrates it | Size |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Declarative provider catalogue** (YAML/TS object per provider: auth mode, URLs, `authorization_params`, `token_params`, `refresh_params`, `scope_separator`, `token_request_auth_method`, `authorization_code_param_in_callback`, `redirect_uri_metadata`, `token_response_metadata`, typed `connection_config` fields with pattern/prefix/suffix/enum, `proxy.base_url/headers` with `${…}` interpolation) | One place per marketplace; new provider = data, not code | `packages/providers/providers.yaml` (shopify, amazon-selling-partner, walmart entries), `packages/types/lib/providers/provider.ts` | M |
| 2 | **Connection health columns**: `credentials_expires_at`, `last_refresh_success/failure`, `refresh_attempts`, `refresh_exhausted`, `last_fetched_at`, `last_execution_at` — plus our own `refresh_token_expires_at` | Lets the UI/cron reason about "needs re-auth" without decrypting tokens | `packages/database/lib/migrations/20250310134848_connection_add_meta_fields.cjs`, `connection.service.ts` `setRefreshFailure` | S |
| 3 | **Refresh-if-needed with buffer, in-flight dedupe, lock, double-check** (`token_expiration_buffer` default 15 min; process map + `SET NX PX` lock; re-read after lock; re-read on lock timeout; keep old refresh_token when rotation omits one) | Prevents the classic "two workers refresh, second invalidates first" with Amazon/eBay | `packages/shared/lib/services/connections/credentials/refresh.ts` 366–582, `oauth2.client.ts` 216–222, `kvstore/lib/Locking.ts` | M |
| 4 | **Failure cooldown + exhaustion** (30-s cooldown, N failed *days* → exhausted; success resets; manual force bypasses) and the **active-error record cleared on recovery with a recovery event** | Stops retry storms; gives "connection broken since …" and "recovered" signals | `refresh.ts` 98–109, `hooks.ts` `connectionRefreshFailed/Success` | S |

#### Not worth cloning

- Multi-tenant accounts/environments/plans/billing/metering/capping; Connect UI + connect sessions + end-user model; Slack/notification services; agent/MCP sessions.
- WebSocket + Redis pub/sub result delivery (the `postMessage` path alone is enough for one origin).
- The five-service topology, per-customer runners (Fleet/Kubernetes/Lambda/Render), `node:vm` sandboxing, script compilation and S3 deploy, `nango.yaml`/zod → JSON-schema pipeline and per-record schema validation flags.
- 256-way hash partitioning, `records_data` blob side table, daily `records_seen` partitions, `records_routing` multi-store, auto-prune/auto-delete daemons, MAR accounting, per-record encryption, KMS envelope encryption.
- ElasticSearch/ClickHouse operation logs and `dd-trace` spans everywhere.
- The 982-provider catalogue as a whole (we hand-write ≈10 entries) and the 17 auth modes (we need OAUTH2, OAUTH2_CC, API_KEY/BASIC).
- The legacy `X-Nango-Signature` scheme, `track_deletes` config flag (use start/end markers), `deleteRecordsFromPreviousExecutions`, `batchSend`.
- Their commerce YAML entries verbatim: shopify/ebay/amazon-selling-partner/etsy/bigcommerce/walmart are correct skeletons but lack rate-limit headers, refresh-token expiry, marketplace ids, RDT — we should write ours with those fields added.

## 19. SOURCE: `docs/cx-research-2026-08-29/R9-references.md`

### R9 — How other platforms model integrations/connectors (reference study for the Nango comparison)

Date: 2026-08-29. Method: WebFetch of GitHub raw files / official docs only; the local repo was not touched. Every claim carries a URL; where a page could not be read it is marked **unverified**. Quotes are ≤10 lines. **Intent is re-implementation of patterns, never copying code** — licences are stated per project so nothing is lifted by accident.

Section 1 (Airbyte) was delivered by a sub-agent and is saved separately: `research-R9a-airbyte.md` (same directory). Headline from it: protocol + Python CDK are MIT, the platform **and the connectors** are ELv2; the `advanced_auth` four-blob OAuth declaration, `AsyncRetriever` for report-style APIs, the `HttpResponseFilter` → `RATE_LIMITED`/`REFRESH_TOKEN_THEN_RETRY` action vocabulary, and per-stream `STATE` checkpoints are the patterns worth carrying forward; the record-only (read side) stream model is the thing it lacks.

#### 2. Saleor — Apps, webhooks, channels

**Licence:** BSD-3-Clause — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/saleor/saleor/main/LICENSE ("Copyright (c) 2020-2023, Saleor Commerce", BSD 3-Clause).

##### 2.1 The App model (`saleor/app/models.py`)
Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/saleor/saleor/main/saleor/app/models.py

- `App`: `uuid` (unique, uuid4), `name` (60), `created_at`, `is_active` (default True), `removed_at` (null), `type` (choices `AppType`, default `LOCAL`; the other value is THIRDPARTY), `identifier` (256, blank), `permissions` M2M→`Permission`, `about_app`, `data_privacy`, `data_privacy_url`, `homepage_url`, `support_url`, `configuration_url`, `app_url`, `manifest_url` (2048), `version`, `audience`, `is_installed` (default True), `author`, `brand_logo_default` (ImageField). Methods `get_permissions()`, `has_perms()`, `has_perm()`.
- `AppToken`: `app` FK, `name` (128, default ""), `auth_token` (128, **unique**), `token_last_4` (4). `set_auth_token()` hashes the token via Django's `make_password()` — i.e. the token is stored **hashed**, only the last four characters remain readable for display.
- `AppExtension`: `app` FK, `label`, `url`, `mount` (256), `target` (128, default `DEFAULT_APP_TARGET`), `permissions` M2M, `http_target_method` (deprecated), `settings` JSON, `identifier` (256, null) — `UniqueConstraint(app, identifier)` + `CheckConstraint(identifier != "")`.
- `AppInstallation`: `uuid`, `app_name`, `manifest_url` (2048), `permissions` M2M, `brand_logo_default`; `set_message()` — a job record that lives while the install is in flight.
- `AppProblem` (newer): `app` FK, `message` (2048), `key` (128), `count` (default 1), `is_critical`, `dismissed`, `dismissed_by_user_email`, `dismissed_by_user` FK; `MAX_PROBLEMS_PER_APP = 100`. A per-app **deduplicated problem ledger** (key + count) that the dashboard surfaces — worth noting for connection health.

##### 2.2 Install flow (`saleor/app/installation_utils.py`)
Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/saleor/saleor/main/saleor/app/installation_utils.py

`install_app()`: `manifest_data = fetch_manifest(app_installation.manifest_url, max_retries=2)` with timeout `settings.COMMON_REQUESTS_TIMEOUT` (a `(connect, read)` tuple, connect timeout grows per retry: `timeout=(connect_timeout + attempt, read_timeout)`); permissions granted are those on the `AppInstallation` (`manifest_data['permissions'] = get_permission_names(assigned_permissions)`) — i.e. the installing user chooses, the manifest only requests; `clean_manifest_data(..., raise_for_saleor_version=True)` validates against `requiredSaleorVersion`; the `App` row is created; a token is created **only if the manifest has `tokenTargetUrl`** (`app.tokens.create(name='Default token')`) and `send_app_token()` POSTs `{'auth_token': token}` with headers `AppHeaders.DOMAIN`, `AppHeaders.API_URL` (= absolute `/graphql/` URL), `AppHeaders.SCHEMA_VERSION` (plus deprecated `X-` twins). If that POST fails the install is **rolled back** (app deleted). Webhooks from the manifest are `bulk_create`d together with their `WebhookEvent` rows; extensions likewise.

Manifest shape (docs): https://docs.saleor.io/developer/extending/apps/architecture/manifest — top-level `id`, `version`, `name`, `author`, `about`, `requiredSaleorVersion`, `appUrl`, `configurationUrl`, `tokenTargetUrl`, `dataPrivacyUrl`, `homepageUrl`, `supportUrl`, `permissions[]`, `brand`, `extensions[]`, `webhooks[]`; each webhook: `name`, `identifier` (stable app-defined key), `asyncEvents[]` or `syncEvents[]`, `query` (GraphQL subscription that **defines the payload**), `targetUrl`, `isActive`; each extension: `label`, `identifier`, `mount` (e.g. `PRODUCT_OVERVIEW_CREATE`), `target` (`POPUP` | `APP_PAGE`), `permissions`, `url`. Condensed example from the docs:
```json
{ "id": "example.app.wonderful", "version": "1.0.0", "name": "My Wonderful App",
  "permissions": ["MANAGE_USERS"], "appUrl": "http://localhost:3001/app",
  "webhooks": [{ "identifier": "order-created", "asyncEvents": ["ORDER_CREATED"],
                 "targetUrl": "https://example.com/api/webhooks" }] }
```

App-side persistence (APL) in `@saleor/app-sdk`: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/saleor/app-sdk/main/src/APL/apl.ts — `AuthData { token, saleorApiUrl, appId, jwks? }`; interface `APL { get(saleorApiUrl), set(authData), delete(saleorApiUrl), getAll(), isReady?(), isConfigured?() }`. The key of the store is the **Saleor API URL** (one app can serve many Saleor instances — multi-tenant by URL).

##### 2.3 Webhooks (`saleor/webhook/`)
Models — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/saleor/saleor/main/saleor/webhook/models.py: `Webhook { name, app FK (related_name webhooks), target_url (WebhookURLField 255), is_active, secret_key (255, null), subscription_query (Text, null), custom_headers (JSON), filterable_channel_slugs (ArrayField, GIN index), identifier (256) }` with `UniqueConstraint(app, identifier)`; `WebhookEvent { webhook FK, event_type (128, indexed) }`. Note `filterable_channel_slugs` — a webhook can be **scoped to channels**.

Event vocabulary — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/saleor/saleor/main/saleor/webhook/event_types.py: `WebhookEventAsyncType` has 113 entries (incl. `ANY`) — e.g. `PRODUCT_CREATED/UPDATED/DELETED`, `PRODUCT_VARIANT_CREATED/UPDATED/STOCK_UPDATED`, `PRODUCT_VARIANT_OUT_OF_STOCK_IN_CHANNEL`, `PRODUCT_MEDIA_CREATED`, `ORDER_CREATED/PAID/FULFILLED/CANCELLED`, `CHANNEL_CREATED/UPDATED`, `APP_INSTALLED`; `WebhookEventSyncType` has 21 — payment authorize/capture/refund/void/confirm/process/list-gateways, `CHECKOUT_CALCULATE_TAXES` / `ORDER_CALCULATE_TAXES`, transaction charge/refund/cancel requested, `SHIPPING_LIST_METHODS_FOR_CHECKOUT`, checkout/order filter-shipping-methods, payment-gateway/transaction session init/process, tokenization, stored-payment-method list/delete. Each event maps to a required permission (`PERMISSIONS` dict); async `EVENT_MAP` flags `is_deferred_payload`. Both classes expose `CHOICES`, `ALL`, `PERMISSIONS`.

Signing — https://docs.saleor.io/developer/extending/webhooks/payload-signature: when no `secretKey` is set Saleor uses "the JWS signature using RS256 with payload detached", sent in `Saleor-Signature` as `header..signature` (RFC 7515 detached), verifiable against `/.well-known/jwks.json`; "If `secretKey` was set for a webhook" it falls back to "the HMAC SHA-256 header based on it and the payload" (deprecated). Other headers (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/saleor/saleor/main/saleor/webhook/transport/utils.py): `Saleor-Event-Type`, `Saleor-Domain`, `Saleor-Signature`, `Saleor-Api-Url` (and deprecated `X-Saleor-*`: "X- headers will be deprecated in Saleor 4.0"). Transport dispatches on the `target_url` scheme: http(s) POST with `settings.WEBHOOK_TIMEOUT`, **AWS SQS**, **Google Pub/Sub** — the same webhook row can target a queue instead of a URL.

Delivery log — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/saleor/saleor/main/saleor/core/models.py: `EventPayload { payload (Text), payload_file (FileField on private storage, null), created_at }` (big payloads go to a file); `EventDelivery { created_at, status (EventDeliveryStatus), event_type, payload FK, webhook FK }`; `EventDeliveryAttempt { delivery FK, created_at, task_id, duration (Float), response, response_headers, response_status_code, request_headers, status }`. Response bodies are capped at `EVENT_DELIVERY_ATTEMPT_RESPONSE_SIZE_LIMIT` with `"..."` appended (transport/utils.py). Async retries — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/saleor/saleor/main/saleor/webhook/transport/asynchronous/transport.py:
```python
@app.task(queue=settings.WEBHOOK_CELERY_QUEUE_NAME, bind=True,
          retry_backoff=10, retry_kwargs={"max_retries": 5})
def send_webhook_request_async(self, event_delivery_id, *, telemetry_context)
```
`countdown = retry_backoff * (2**retries)`; 3xx/4xx responses **do not retry** (only 5xx / network), `MAX_WEBHOOK_RETRIES = 5`, `WEBHOOK_ASYNC_BATCH_SIZE = 100`, per-app batching task `send_webhooks_async_for_app`, deferred payload generation task with `max_retries=12`. Every attempt is reported to an observability buffer (`observability.report_event_delivery_attempt`). Sync webhooks — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/saleor/saleor/main/saleor/webhook/transport/synchronous/transport.py: `settings.WEBHOOK_SYNC_TIMEOUT` (docs: 2 s connect + 18 s read, https://docs.saleor.io/developer/extending/webhooks/overview), response `json.loads`ed and returned only on `SUCCESS`; responses cached under a key of (cache_data, url, event, app) for `WEBHOOK_CACHE_DEFAULT_TTL`; a failure stores `SYNC_WEBHOOK_FAILURE_SENTINEL` for `SYNC_WEBHOOK_FAILURE_CACHE_TTL` ("Prevent sending webhook if the previous one failed recently"); sync calls are wrapped by a `breaker_board` **circuit breaker**; EventDelivery/Attempt rows are still written for sync calls. Retention — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/saleor/saleor/main/saleor/core/tasks.py: `delete_event_payloads_task` deletes payloads (and their files) whose deliveries are older than `EVENT_PAYLOAD_DELETE_PERIOD`, `BATCH_SIZE = 1000` ("tested on db with 1mln payloads and deliveries").

##### 2.4 Channels and channel listings
`Channel` — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/saleor/saleor/main/saleor/channel/models.py: `ModelWithMetadata` + `name`, `slug` (unique), `is_active`, `currency_code`, `default_country`, `allocation_strategy`, `order_mark_as_paid_strategy`, `default_transaction_flow_strategy`, order settings (`automatically_confirm_all_new_orders`, `allow_unpaid_orders`, `expire_orders_after`, `delete_expired_orders_after` …), checkout settings (`automatically_complete_fully_paid_checkouts`, `checkout_ttl_before_releasing_funds` …). One currency per channel.

Listings — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/saleor/saleor/main/saleor/product/models.py: `ProductChannelListing { product FK, channel FK, visible_in_listings, available_for_purchase_at, currency, discounted_price_amount, discounted_price_dirty }`, `unique_together (product, channel)`, `is_available_for_purchase()`; `ProductVariantChannelListing { variant FK, channel FK, currency, price_amount, cost_price_amount, prior_price_amount, discounted_price_amount, promotion_rules M2M (through VariantChannelListingPromotionRule), preorder_quantity_threshold }`, `unique_together (variant, channel)`; `CollectionChannelListing { collection, channel }`. `Product` itself keeps only channel-independent fields (`name`, `slug`, `description`, `category`, `weight`, `rating`, `tax_class` …). Docs confirm the scope list — products (visibility/availability/publication), variant prices, vouchers, promotions, orders ("contextualized to a channel and required channel permission for access"), warehouses/shipping zones availability, shipping rates, tax config, payment flow settings: https://docs.saleor.io/developer/channels/overview. `ChannelContext(node, channel_slug)` wrapper in GraphQL resolvers — **unverified** (fetch of `saleor/graphql/channel/__init__.py` returned no content).

Pre-App extension pattern — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/saleor/saleor/main/saleor/plugins/models.py: `PluginConfiguration { identifier (128), name, channel FK (null), description, active (default False), configuration (JSON) }` with `unique (identifier, channel)` — a plugin's config is **per channel**. Generic escape hatch: `ModelWithMetadata` gives every entity `metadata` and `private_metadata` JSONB (`db_default={}`) with `store_value_in_metadata` / `get_value_from_metadata` helpers (core/models.py).

##### 2.5 What Saleor gets right / loses
- Right: the **install handshake** (manifest → permissions chosen by installer → token POSTed to `tokenTargetUrl`, rollback on failure); **payload-by-subscription-query** (the receiver chooses fields, so payload schema drift is the app's problem, not the core's); **three-table delivery log** (payload / delivery / attempt) with per-attempt request+response headers, duration and status; **channel-scoped webhooks**; sync webhooks with cache + failure sentinel + breaker.
- Loses: apps are **outbound receivers only** — there is no inbound "connector sync" concept, no cursor/state model, no rate-limit vocabulary; channel listing is **one row per (entity, channel) with a fixed column set** — a channel cannot carry arbitrary per-channel attributes (Amazon product-type attributes, eBay item specifics) except via untyped `metadata`; `metadata` is an untyped JSON bag with no schema or validation; delivery payloads are deleted after `EVENT_PAYLOAD_DELETE_PERIOD` so the log is not an audit trail.

#### 3. Medusa v2 — sales channels, workflows, links, events, providers

**Licence:** MIT — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/medusajs/medusa/develop/LICENSE ("Copyright (c) 2021 Medusajs"; the LICENSE notes Enterprise Edition material is under a separate `ENTERPRISE-LICENSE.md`).

##### 3.1 Sales Channel module
`SalesChannel` model — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/medusajs/medusa/develop/packages/modules/sales-channel/src/models/sales-channel.ts: `id` (prefix `sc`), `name` (searchable), `description` (nullable), `is_disabled` (default false), `metadata` (JSON). Products are attached by a **link module**, not a FK — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/medusajs/medusa/develop/packages/modules/link-modules/src/definitions/product-sales-channel.ts: `serviceName: "product_sales_channel"`, `isLink: true`, `databaseConfig { tableName: "product_sales_channel", idPrefix: "prodsc" }`, `primaryKeys: ["id","product_id","sales_channel_id"]`, relationships to `Modules.PRODUCT`/`Product` and `Modules.SALES_CHANNEL`/`SalesChannel`, and `extends` so Product exposes `sales_channels` and SalesChannel exposes `products_link`. Docs — https://docs.medusajs.com/resources/commerce-modules/sales-channel: "specify a product's availability per sales channel", carts "are scoped to a sales channel", stock locations linked to channels for availability. **There is no per-channel product data (title/price) — membership only.** Pricing rules — https://docs.medusajs.com/resources/commerce-modules/pricing/price-rules — take attributes like `region.id`, `customer.groups.id`, `shipping_address.country_code`, `item_total` and custom attributes; `sales_channel_id` is **not** a built-in rule attribute (a custom attribute could be added).

##### 3.2 Workflows engine (saga with compensation)
Composer — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/medusajs/medusa/develop/packages/core/workflows-sdk/src/utils/composer/create-step.ts: `createStep(nameOrConfig, invokeFn, compensateFn?)`; the first arg may be `{ name, maxRetries, ... }` (any `TransactionStepsDefinition` field except `next`/`uuid`/`action`); `new StepResponse(output, compensateInput)` — the second arg is what the compensation receives (defaults to the first); `StepResponse.permanentFailure(message, partialData)` hands partial progress to the compensation (docs caveat for loops: https://docs.medusajs.com/learn/fundamentals/workflows/compensation-function). Compensation runs only on error and **in reverse order** of completed steps (same page). Doc example (≤10 lines):
```ts
return new StepResponse(
  `Hello from step one!`,
  { message: "Oops! Rolling back my changes..." }
)
// compensation: async ({ message }, { container }) => { console.log(message) }
```
Step definition knobs — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/medusajs/medusa/develop/packages/core/orchestration/src/transaction/types.ts: `continueOnPermanentFailure`, `skipOnPermanentFailure` (bool | string), `noCompensation`, `maxRetries` (default 0), `autoRetry` (default true), `retryInterval` (s), `retryIntervalAwaiting`, `maxAwaitingRetries`, `timeout` (s), `async` ("Workflow will not wait for the response of this step"), `nested`, `backgroundExecution`, `compensateAsync`, `noWait`, `saveResponse` (default true), `store` (checkpoint). Orchestrator events: `BEGIN, RESUME, COMPENSATE_BEGIN, FINISH, TIMEOUT, STEP_BEGIN, STEP_SUCCESS, STEP_SKIPPED, STEP_FAILURE, STEP_AWAITING, COMPENSATE_STEP_SUCCESS, COMPENSATE_STEP_FAILURE`. The `TransactionState`/`TransactionStepStatus` enum values themselves live in `@medusajs/utils` — **unverified** (not fetched).

Long-running workflows — https://docs.medusajs.com/learn/fundamentals/workflows/long-running-workflow: a step with `async: true` that does not return a `StepResponse` parks the transaction; `run()` returns `transaction.transactionId`; the external system later calls `workflowEngineService.setStepSuccess({ idempotencyKey: { transactionId, stepId, workflowId }, stepResponse })` or `setStepFailure(...)` (which triggers compensation of earlier steps); `subscribe()` streams `onFinish` / `onStepFailure`. Persistence — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/medusajs/medusa/develop/packages/modules/workflow-engine-redis/src/models/workflow-execution.ts: `WorkflowExecution { id, workflow_id, transaction_id, run_id, execution, context, state, retention_time }`, composite PK `(workflow_id, transaction_id, run_id)`, indexes on `state`, `(state, updated_at)`, `(retention_time, updated_at, state)` for retention sweeps, all with `deleted_at IS NULL`.

##### 3.3 Modules & Module Links
https://docs.medusajs.com/learn/fundamentals/module-links: `defineLink(ProductModule.linkable.product, BlogModule.linkable.post)`; one-to-many by wrapping a side in `{ linkable, isList: true }` (both sides for many-to-many); `deleteCascade`; link rows created/removed with `link.create` / `link.delete`; cross-module reads go through `query.graph({ entity: "product", fields: ["id", "featured_post.*"] })`. Isolation rule: "you can't access another module's data models to add a relation to it" — links are separate tables with **no FK constraints** across modules. Extra columns on link tables exist (`database.extraColumns`) but the page fetched only references the chapter — **unverified** detail. This is the mechanism by which a plugin could hang per-channel data off a product without touching the product module.

##### 3.4 Event bus & subscribers
https://docs.medusajs.com/learn/fundamentals/events-and-subscribers: a subscriber file default-exports `async function handler({ event: { data }, container })` and `export const config: SubscriberConfig = { event: "product.created" }` (or an array of events); two event modules ship — Local (default) and Redis (production). `emit(events, { eventGroupId })`, `releaseGroupedEvents` / `clearGroupedEvents` (events buffered per transaction and released on commit) — **unverified** (the fetch of `abstract-event-bus-module-service.ts` hit the session limit).

##### 3.5 Provider abstractions (per-capability plug-ins)
- Fulfillment — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/medusajs/medusa/develop/packages/core/utils/src/fulfillment/provider.ts: `static identifier`; `getFulfillmentOptions()`, `validateFulfillmentData(optionData, data, context)`, `validateOption(data)`, `canCalculate(data)`, `calculatePrice(optionData, data, context)`, `createFulfillment(data, items, order, fulfillment, additionalData)`, `cancelFulfillment(data)`, `getFulfillmentDocuments`, `createReturnFulfillment`, `getReturnDocuments`, `getShipmentDocuments`, `retrieveDocuments(fulfillmentData, documentType)`.
- Payment — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/medusajs/medusa/develop/packages/core/utils/src/payment/abstract-payment-provider.ts: `static identifier`, `static validateOptions(options)`, `constructor(cradle, config)` ("If you're creating a client … do it in the constructor"); abstract `initiatePayment, authorizePayment, capturePayment, refundPayment, cancelPayment, deletePayment, getPaymentStatus, retrievePayment, updatePayment, getWebhookActionAndData`.
- Notification — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/medusajs/medusa/develop/packages/core/utils/src/notification/abstract-notification-provider.ts: `static identifier`, `static validateOptions`, `send(notification: ProviderSendNotificationDTO): Promise<ProviderSendNotificationResultsDTO>`.
- Registration — https://docs.medusajs.com/resources/references/fulfillment/provider:
```ts
{ resolve: "@medusajs/medusa/fulfillment",
  options: { providers: [
    { resolve: "./src/modules/my-fulfillment", id: "my-fulfillment", options: {} } ] } }
```
"The provider's ID will be stored as `fp_{identifier}_{id}`"; shipping options in a location/service zone reference it via `provider_id` — so a provider is enabled **per stock location**, which is the closest Medusa gets to "per-channel provider".
- Plugins — https://docs.medusajs.com/learn/fundamentals/plugins: a plugin bundles "Modules, API Routes, Workflows, Workflow Hooks, Links, Subscribers, Scheduled Jobs, and Admin Extensions" and is published to npm.

##### 3.6 What Medusa gets right / loses
- Right: **compensating sagas with persisted state and external resume** (`setStepSuccess` with an idempotency key) — exactly the shape of "push to Amazon, wait for the feed result, then continue or roll back"; **module links** as a way to attach data across bounded contexts without FKs; providers as classes with a static `identifier` + `validateOptions` + constructor-time client init; event grouping tied to the transaction.
- Loses: sales channel is **membership-only** — no per-channel title/price/attributes; providers are per **capability** (fulfillment/payment/notification), not per **marketplace**, so a "Shopify provider" has no home; no inbound connector/sync/cursor/rate-limit model at all; workflow engine state in Redis by default (a separate module for Postgres/in-memory exists — not verified here).

---

#### 4. Supaglue · Panora · Revert — unified model + raw payload

##### 4.1 Supaglue
- Status: **archived**, last push 2024-03-07, 427 stars, MIT — https://api.github.com/repos/supaglue-labs/supaglue; LICENSE https://raw.githubusercontent.com/supaglue-labs/supaglue/main/LICENSE (MIT, "copyright 2023 Supergrain, Inc."). README (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/supaglue-labs/supaglue/main/README.md) describes three modes: managed syncs into your DB, an Actions API (read/write), real-time webhooks.
- Destination column contract — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/supaglue-labs/supaglue/main/packages/core/destination_writers/postgres.ts: every synced table gets `_supaglue_application_id`, `_supaglue_provider_name`, `_supaglue_customer_id`, `_supaglue_id`, `_supaglue_emitted_at`, `_supaglue_last_modified_at`, `_supaglue_is_deleted`, `_supaglue_raw_data`, `_supaglue_mapped_data`, and `_supaglue_object_name` for custom objects; composite `PRIMARY KEY ("_supaglue_application_id", "_supaglue_provider_name", "_supaglue_customer_id", "_supaglue_id"[, "_supaglue_object_name"])`; writes stage into a `temp_`-prefixed table indexed on `(_supaglue_id ASC, _supaglue_last_modified_at DESC)` before merging. **Raw and mapped live side by side in the same row** — the key pattern.
- Schema — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/supaglue-labs/supaglue/main/packages/db/prisma/schema.prisma: `Provider { authType, category, name, config, objects, entityMappings, hubspotAppId }`; `Connection { category, providerName, status, credentials, customerId, instanceUrl, replayIds, providerId, schemaMappingsConfig, entityMappings, connectionSyncConfig }`; `Sync { type, objectType, object, entityId, state, strategy, connectionId, paused, syncConfigId, argsForNextRun }`; `SyncRun { status, errorMessage, strategy, startTimestamp, endTimestamp, numRecordsSynced }`; `Destination { type, encryptedConfig, version }`; `SyncConfig { providerId, destinationId, config }`; `Schema`, `Entity` (customer-defined objects), plus change-tracking tables `SyncConfigChange`, `ConnectionSyncConfigChange`, `SyncChange`. Strategy values `full_then_incremental` / `full_only` and `period_ms` are in `SyncConfig.config` JSON — **unverified** at field level (JSON blob not read).
- Lost by unifying: anything outside the common object needs `entityMappings`/`schemaMappingsConfig` (customer-defined "Entities" mapped per connection), and the unified write side was a thin "Actions API"; the company shut down (archived repo).

##### 4.2 Panora
- Status: **archived**, last push 2025-10-26, 1,034 stars, AGPL-3.0 — https://api.github.com/repos/panoratech/Panora; LICENSE https://raw.githubusercontent.com/panoratech/Panora/main/LICENSE (GNU AGPL v3, 19 Nov 2007).
- Schema — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/panoratech/Panora/main/packages/api/prisma/schema.prisma: `connections { id_connection, status, provider_slug, vertical, account_url, token_type, access_token, refresh_token, expiration_timestamp, connection_token, id_linked_user, id_project }`; `linked_users { linked_user_origin_id, alias, id_project }` (the customer's end user); `projects { sync_mode, pull_frequency, redirect_url, id_connector_set }`; **`remote_data { id_remote_data, ressource_owner_id, format, data, created_at }`** — raw payload stored in a **separate table keyed by the unified row id**, not inline; unified rows carry `remote_id`, `remote_platform`, `id_connection` (e.g. `crm_contacts`); `events { type, status, direction, method, url, provider, id_linked_user }` (an API-call ledger); `webhook_endpoints { url, secret, active, scope }`, `webhook_delivery_attempts { status, next_retry, attempt_count, id_webhooks_payload, id_event }`; `managed_webhooks { id_connection, endpoint, api_version, active_events, remote_signing_secret }` (provider→Panora inbound); field mappings as EAV: `attribute { slug, data_type, remote_id, source, id_entity, scope }`, `value { data, id_entity, id_attribute }`, `entity { ressource_owner_id }`.
- Provider catalogue — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/panoratech/Panora/main/packages/shared/src/connectors/metadata.ts: map keyed by vertical then slug; each has `scopes`, `urls { docsUrl, apiUrl (may be a function of store name), authBaseUrl, customPropertiesUrl }`, `logoPath`, `description`, `active`, `authStrategy { strategy: oauth2 | api_key | basic, properties? }`, `primaryColor`, `options { local_redirect_uri_in_https, company_subdomain, end_user_domain }`, rare `realTimeWebhookMetadata`. Ecommerce vertical lists BigCommerce, eBay, Squarespace, Amazon, Shopify, Magento, Webflow, Faire, Mercado Libre, WooCommerce. Shopify entry: `apiUrl: (storeName) => \`https://${storeName}.myshopify.com\``, `authStrategy: {strategy: api_key, properties: ['api_key','store_url']}` — i.e. Panora never did Shopify OAuth, it took an Admin API token.
- Lost by unifying: custom fields become an EAV triple; passthrough exists (`/passthrough`, **unverified** — docs not fetched); the ecommerce vertical covered products/orders/customers/fulfilments only (the connector list shows breadth over depth).

##### 4.3 Revert
- Status: not archived, last push 2025-04-07, 1,012 stars, AGPL-3.0 — https://api.github.com/repos/revertinc/revert; README says "Revert has joined Ampersand" and directs users there — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revertinc/revert/main/README.md. LICENSE file at `/LICENSE` returned 404 (GitHub's licence metadata says AGPL-3.0) — file **unverified**.
- Schema — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revertinc/revert/main/packages/backend/prisma/schema.prisma: `connections { tp_id, tp_access_token, tp_refresh_token, tp_customer_id, t_id, tp_account_url, owner_account_public_token, app_client_id, app_client_secret, app_config, appId, schema_mapping_id, environmentId }` — `t_id` is the tenant, `tp_*` the third party; `apps { tp_id, scope, app_client_id, app_client_secret, app_config, env, is_revert_app }` (bring-your-own OAuth app vs Revert's); `accounts`/`environments` each with `private_token`/`public_token`; `fieldMappings { source_tp_id, source_field_name, target_field_name, is_standard_field, schema_id }`; `accountFieldMappingConfig { allow_connection_override_custom_fields, mappable_by_connection_field_list }`. `TP_ID` enum: hubspot, zohocrm, sfdc, pipedrive, closecrm, ms_dynamics_365_sales, slack, discord, linear, clickup, asana, trello, jira, bitbucket, quickbooks, xero, greenhouse, lever, github — **no commerce providers**.
- Model: proxy-style unified API with "automatic OAuth token refresh" and "API retry mechanism" (README); no sync engine. Lost: no commerce at all, and the team pivoted.

##### 4.4 Cross-cutting lesson
All three keep the raw payload (Supaglue inline `_supaglue_raw_data`; Panora in a `remote_data` side table; Merge as `remote_data[]` — §6.1) and all three had to bolt on a **field-mapping layer** (Supaglue `entityMappings`, Panora EAV `attribute/value`, Revert `fieldMappings` + per-account override policy) because the common model could not carry provider-specific fields. Two of three are archived. A PIM that needs 100% channel coverage should **start** from the provider's full schema and derive a thin common view, not the reverse.

#### 5. Shopify — OAuth, sessions, webhooks, scopes, token exchange (`@shopify/shopify-api`)

**Licence:** MIT — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Shopify/shopify-app-js/main/LICENSE.md ("Copyright (c) 2022-present, Shopify Inc."). The Remix template's licence file was not readable at `/LICENSE.md` or `/LICENSE` (404) — **unverified** (repo metadata says MIT).

##### 5.1 `begin()` / `callback()` — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Shopify/shopify-app-js/main/packages/apps/shopify-api/lib/auth/oauth/oauth.ts
- `begin({shop, callbackPath, isOnline})`: `nonce()` → state; state stored in a **signed** cookie `STATE_COOKIE_NAME` (`shopify_app_state`) with `sameSite: 'lax'`, `secure: true`, `expires: new Date(Date.now() + 60000)` (60 s), path = callback path; authorization URL query = `client_id: config.apiKey`, `scope` (comma-joined), `redirect_uri`, `state`, and `grant_options[]: 'per-user'` for online tokens; bots (`isbot(userAgent)`) get HTTP 410.
- `callback()`: `await cookies.getAndVerify(STATE_COOKIE_NAME)` then delete it; `validQuery()` = `await validateHmac(config)(query)` **and** `safeCompare(query.state!, stateFromCookie)`; `sanitizeShop(config)(query.shop)`; `POST https://${cleanShop}/admin/oauth/access_token` with `client_id`, `client_secret`, `code`, `expiring: '1' | '0'`; `createSession()`; for non-embedded apps a `SESSION_COOKIE_NAME` cookie (`lax`, `secure`). Errors: `InvalidOAuthError` (HMAC/state), `CookieNotFound`, `BotActivityDetected`.
- HMAC — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Shopify/shopify-app-js/main/packages/apps/shopify-api/lib/utils/hmac-validator.ts: drop `hmac` and `signature` keys, sort keys, stringify (`ProcessedQuery` for admin, `key=value` joined for app-proxy), HMAC-SHA256 hex with the API secret, `safeCompare`; `timestamp` must be within `HMAC_TIMESTAMP_PERMITTED_CLOCK_TOLERANCE_SEC` = 90 s.
- Shop regex — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Shopify/shopify-app-js/main/packages/apps/shopify-api/lib/utils/shop-validator.ts: `^[a-zA-Z0-9][a-zA-Z0-9-_]*\.(domain)[/]*$` with domain ∈ `myshopify.com | shopify.com | myshopify.io | shop.dev` (+ configured `domainTransformations`); `sanitizeShop` also rewrites `admin.{domain}/store/{shop}` to the legacy form and returns `null` or throws `InvalidShopError`; `sanitizeHost` base64-decodes and checks the suffix.

##### 5.2 Session model — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Shopify/shopify-app-js/main/packages/apps/shopify-api/lib/session/session.ts
`Session { id (readonly), shop, state, isOnline, scope?, expires?, accessToken?, refreshToken?, refreshTokenExpires?, onlineAccessInfo? }`; `isActive(scopes)` = "Active sessions have an access token that is not expired, and has the given scopes"; `isExpired(withinMs)`; `isScopeChanged(scopes)`; `isScopeIncluded(scopes)` via `AuthScopes`; `toPropertyArray(returnUserData)` / `fromPropertyArray()` flatten `onlineAccessInfo` for storage adapters; `equals()`. Id conventions `offline_{shop}` / `{shop}_{userId}` — **unverified** here (the id-builder file was not fetched; the Prisma template and docs use `offline_` prefixes). Prisma adapter schema — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Shopify/shopify-app-js/main/packages/apps/session-storage/shopify-app-session-storage-prisma/prisma/schema.prisma:
```prisma
model Session { id String @id; shop String; state String; isOnline Boolean @default(false)
  scope String?; expires DateTime?; accessToken String; userId BigInt?
  firstName String?; lastName String?; email String?; accountOwner Boolean?
  locale String?; collaborator Boolean?; emailVerified Boolean?
  refreshToken String?; refreshTokenExpires DateTime? }
```

##### 5.3 Webhooks
- Register — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Shopify/shopify-app-js/main/packages/apps/shopify-api/lib/webhooks/register.ts: queries `webhookSubscriptions` (250/page), diffs existing vs configured handlers with `handlerIdentifier()` and `areHandlerFieldsEqual()` (`includeFields`, `metafieldNamespaces`) into create / update / delete; mutation prefix by delivery method — HTTP `webhookSubscription…` (`callbackUrl`), EventBridge `eventBridgeWebhookSubscription…` (`arn`), PubSub `pubSubWebhookSubscription…` (`pubSubProject`, `pubSubTopic`); returns `{[topic]: [{deliveryMethod, success, result, operation}]}` with success = `userErrors.length === 0`; privacy topics skipped; leftovers deleted. **Reconciliation, not append** — the desired set is the source of truth.
- Process — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Shopify/shopify-app-js/main/packages/apps/shopify-api/lib/webhooks/process.ts: requires headers Hmac, Topic, Domain, WebhookId, ApiVersion; "base64 HMAC-SHA256 with apiSecretKey" over the raw body + safeCompare; handler lookup `webhookRegistry[topic]`; 401 "Could not validate request HMAC", 404 "No HTTP webhooks registered for topic", 400 missing headers/body, 500 on handler error; callback gets `(topic, domain, rawBody, webhookId, apiVersion, context)`.
- Template — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Shopify/shopify-app-template-remix/main/shopify.app.toml: `[access_scopes] scopes = "write_products"`; `[webhooks] api_version = "2024-10"`; `[[webhooks.subscriptions]] topics = ["app/uninstalled"] uri = "/webhooks/app/uninstalled"` and `["app/scopes_update"] → "/webhooks/app/scopes_update"`; commented examples for `products/update` with `filter = "variants.price:>=10.00"` and compliance topics. App-level subscriptions in TOML are created by Shopify at deploy for **every** shop; API-registered ones are per shop. Handlers: uninstall — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Shopify/shopify-app-template-remix/main/app/routes/webhooks.app.uninstalled.tsx:
```ts
const { shop, session, topic } = await authenticate.webhook(request);
if (session) { await db.session.deleteMany({ where: { shop } }); }
```
scopes_update — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Shopify/shopify-app-template-remix/main/app/routes/webhooks.app.scopes_update.tsx:
```ts
const current = payload.current as string[];
if (session) { await db.session.update({ where: { id: session.id },
  data: { scope: current.toString() } }); }
```

##### 5.4 Scopes — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Shopify/shopify-app-js/main/packages/apps/shopify-api/lib/auth/scopes/index.ts
`AuthScopes` accepts string/array/instance; trims and drops empties; computes implied scopes — every `write_(.*)` implies the matching `read_`, preserving an `unauthenticated_` prefix; keeps three sets (compressed = non-implied, expanded, original); `has()`, `equals()` (compare compressed), `toArray()`, `toString()`. No `_orders` special case seen in this file.

##### 5.5 Token exchange, managed install, client credentials
- Token exchange — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Shopify/shopify-app-js/main/packages/apps/shopify-api/lib/auth/oauth/token-exchange.ts and https://shopify.dev/docs/apps/build/authentication-authorization/access-tokens/token-exchange: `RequestedTokenType` = `urn:shopify:params:oauth:token-type:online-access-token` | `…:offline-access-token`; body `client_id, client_secret, grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange, subject_token=<App Bridge ID token>, subject_token_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:id_token, requested_token_type, expiring`; the JWT is validated first (`decodeSessionToken`); "Embedded apps … use this grant to exchange an ID token for an access token, without redirecting the merchant"; "ID tokens are short-lived, so request one per exchange instead of caching it"; a stale token yields 400 → fetch a fresh one and retry.
- ID (session) token claims — https://shopify.dev/docs/apps/build/authentication-authorization/session-tokens: `iss` (admin host), `dest` (shop domain), `aud` (client id), `sub` (user), `exp`, `nbf`, `iat`, `jti`, `sid`; HS256 with the app secret; "they expire one minute after they're issued".
- Managed installation — https://shopify.dev/docs/apps/build/authentication-authorization/app-installation: declaring `[access_scopes] scopes` in TOML makes Shopify own the install/consent screen; "If you add scopes later, merchants who already have your app installed approve the new ones the next time they open it"; the app then does token exchange and sends `X-Shopify-Access-Token` on every request.
- Client credentials (own-org apps) — https://shopify.dev/docs/apps/build/authentication-authorization/access-tokens/client-credentials-grant: `grant_type=client_credentials` + `client_id` + `client_secret`; `expires_in` "Always 86399 (24 hours)"; cache and refresh ~60 s before expiry.

##### 5.6 Rate limits & client
https://shopify.dev/docs/api/usage/rate-limits: GraphQL is cost-based — "Each combination of app and store is given a bucket size and restore rate based on API and plan tier" (100/200/1000/2000 points·s⁻¹ restore), `extensions.cost { requestedQueryCost, actualQueryCost, throttleStatus { maximumAvailable, currentlyAvailable, restoreRate } }`, single query ≤ 1,000 points; bulk operations "don't have the max cost limits or rate limits that single queries have". Client — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Shopify/shopify-app-js/main/packages/api-clients/admin-api-client/README.md: `retries` default 0, max 3; retries on 429/503 honouring `Retry-After`; `customFetchApi`; `apiVersion` required, overridable per request.

##### 5.7 What Shopify gets right / to avoid
- Right: signed short-lived state cookie + HMAC over the sorted query + 90 s timestamp window + timing-safe compare; a **sanitised shop regex** as the tenant key; `Session` as the single persisted object with `isActive(scopes)` deciding re-auth; webhook registration as **reconcile-to-desired-state**; `app/uninstalled` and `app/scopes_update` as first-class lifecycle topics; token exchange removes the redirect entirely for embedded apps.
- Avoid: online vs offline duality leaks into every storage adapter (17 columns); `scope` stored as a comma string; `expiring` offline tokens now add `refreshToken`/`refreshTokenExpires` — model expiry from day one.

#### 6. Commercial platforms — one paragraph each (proprietary; pattern only)

##### 6.1 Merge.dev
Pattern: category-scoped Common Models; `include_remote_data=true` returns `remote_data: [{ path, data }]` — the raw third-party response per endpoint, "only available to customers on our Professional or Enterprise plans", not normalised, and refreshed "only if there's a change to Common Model field" (https://docs.merge.dev/supplemental-data/remote-data/). Field Mapping adds target fields on Common Models at integration-wide or Linked-Account level, resolved via `remote_field.field_key` / `field_traversal_path`, surfaced as `field_mappings` and `remote_fields` on responses (https://docs.merge.dev/supplemental-data/field-mappings/overview/). Passthrough: `POST https://api.merge.dev/api/{CATEGORY}/passthrough` with `method, path, base_url_override, data, multipart_form_data, headers, request_format (JSON|XML|MULTIPART), normalize_response`, response `{status, response, headers}`, plus async passthrough (https://docs.merge.dev/merge-unified/supplemental-data/passthrough-request/passthrough-requests.md). Common Model scopes, `/meta/post`, and webhook pages returned 404 — **unverified**.
Loses: no commerce category at all; `remote_data` only refreshes when a Common Model field changes, so provider-only fields go stale; anything outside the model is a paid add-on (Field Mapping, Remote Data, Passthrough are all Professional/Enterprise) — the "unified" layer is where the coverage stops.

##### 6.2 Rutter
Pattern: commerce+accounting unified objects; `Product { id, platform_id, name, description, status (active|archived|inactive|draft), variants[], images, tags, created_at, updated_at, platform_data }` — `platform_data` is the raw-payload field; `access_token` per connection as a query param; list params `force_fetch` ("Bypasses sync checks"), `updated_at_min/max`, `cursor`, `limit` (https://docs.rutter.com/rest/2024-08-31/products). Long-running writes return a Job: `status` "One of prequeued, pending, success, or failure", `response`, `request`, polled via `GET /jobs/:id` or delivered by webhook (https://docs.rutter.com/rest/2024-08-31/jobs). Platform-support matrix and webhooks pages 404 — **unverified**.
Loses: the product model has no per-marketplace attribute dictionary (no Amazon product type, no eBay aspects), `platform_data` is opaque, and reads are served from Rutter's cache (`force_fetch` exists precisely because the cache lags) — a PIM would be reconciling against a stale mirror of a stale mirror.

##### 6.3 Apideck
Pattern: Unify APIs (Ecommerce = Orders, Products, Customers, Stores; https://developers.apideck.com/apis/ecommerce/reference) over a Vault that owns credentials: headers `x-apideck-app-id`, `x-apideck-consumer-id`, `x-apideck-service-id`; Connection `{ id, service_id, unified_api, auth_type (oauth2|apiKey|basic|custom), state (available|callable|added|authorized|invalid), configuration[] per resource, custom_mappings[], enabled, oauth_grant_type, validation_support, schema_support }`; hosted UI via `POST /vault/sessions` → `session_uri`; custom mappings at `/vault/custom-mappings/{unified_api}/{service_id}/{target_field_id}` with expressions like `$['root']['field']`; per-resource downstream config at `/vault/connections/{unified_api}/{service_id}/{resource}/config` (https://developers.apideck.com/apis/vault/reference). Proxy: single `/proxy` endpoint with `x-apideck-downstream-url`, `x-apideck-downstream-authorization`, `x-apideck-downstream-method`, credentials injected from Vault (https://developers.apideck.com/apis/proxy/reference). `raw=true` / `pass_through` / `downstream_error` — **unverified** on the pages fetched.
Loses: the Ecommerce unified API is four read-mostly resources; the "state machine" of a connection (`callable`/`authorized`/`invalid`) is the reusable idea, but coverage of listing attributes is nil — the proxy is the only way to reach them, at which point Apideck is just an OAuth vault.

##### 6.4 Paragon
Pattern: per-integration Workflows built in a UI or in TypeScript ("Paragraph") — "you can switch between the UI and code at any time" (https://docs.useparagon.com/workflows/overview); a Connect Portal where the end user authenticates and sets **User Settings** at integration- or workflow-level (e.g. pick a Slack channel or Salesforce stage), read in workflows via `{{` variables (https://docs.useparagon.com/connect-portal/workflow-user-settings). Field Mapping UI, Task History/replay and the Custom Integration Builder pages 404 — **unverified**.
Loses: the unit is a workflow per (integration, event), not a per-channel data model; user-level field mapping solves "which of *their* fields is our SKU" but not "which of *Amazon's* 400 attributes this product type requires" — coverage is whatever someone drew in the builder.

##### 6.5 Prismatic
Pattern: Connections are a config-variable type ("Connections contain the information necessary for the steps in your integration to connect to third-party apps and services") supporting API key, OAuth 2.0 (`authorizeUrl`, `tokenUrl`, `scopes`) and basic auth; four ownership types — Customer, Organization (per-customer), Organization (global), Integration-scoped (on-prem agents); the platform refreshes tokens before expiry; "connection throttled" is an alert condition (https://prismatic.io/docs/integrations/connections/). Each customer deploys an **Instance** through a config wizard ("multiple configuration pages with dynamically generated dropdown menus, toggles, text fields") with data sources for dynamic dropdowns (https://prismatic.io/docs/integrations/config-wizard/). Alert Monitors pair triggers (execution failed, duration exceeded, log level, connection throttled/failed, instance enabled/succeeded) with email/Slack/PagerDuty/webhook groups (https://prismatic.io/docs/monitor-instances/alerting/).
Loses: an iPaaS for shipping many customers' integrations, not a data model — products/listings are just JSON flowing through steps; nothing enforces channel schema completeness; retention of step results not documented on the pages read (**unverified**).

##### 6.6 ChannelEngine
Pattern: merchant-side REST API authenticated by an `apikey` (query param or header), tenant base URL `https://{tenant}.channelengine.net/api`, resource groups products, offers, channels, orders, shipments, returns, webhooks, product bundles, notifications; the official PHP client is "no longer supported by ChannelEngine" and users are told to generate from the Swagger spec (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/channelengine/merchant-api-client-php/master/README.md). The product request model (`MerchantProductNo`, `ExtraData[] {Key, Value, Type, IsPublic}`, `CategoryTrail` …) and the per-channel product validation/`ChannelErrors` — **unverified**: apidocs.channelengine.net and developers.channelengine.net both redirect to an OIDC login (fetched 2026-08-29).
Loses: the merchant pushes one feed and ChannelEngine's own channel connectors do the per-marketplace mapping — the merchant never sees the marketplace's attribute schema, so "100% coverage" is bounded by what ChannelEngine chose to map, and errors come back post-hoc per channel.

##### 6.7 Feedonomics
Pattern: feed management — "Transform wild product data into optimized listings for 2,000+ destinations", "1.6M+ data governance rules monthly", "100M+ data transformations monthly", AI enrichment/categorisation, monitoring, order orchestration and platform sync (BigCommerce, Shopify, NetSuite, SFCC, Magento) (https://feedonomics.com/). Transformer rule syntax, export mapping UI and the API (`developers.feedonomics.com` / `help.feedonomics.com` — DNS did not resolve on 2026-08-29) — **unverified**.
Loses: it is a *feed* model — flat rows out, per-destination column mapping — with no bidirectional listing state (no "this ASIN is suppressed because attribute X is missing" loop back into the product record); a PIM needs the channel's rejection to land on the product, not in a feed report.

##### 6.8 Rithum / ChannelAdvisor
Pattern (from memory of the public developer docs, marked **unverified** because https://developer.channeladvisor.com/* now redirects to a JavaScript knowledge-center shell that returned no article body): application id + shared secret from a developer console; a per-account authorisation grants a long-lived `refresh_token`; `POST /oauth2/token` with Basic auth and `grant_type=refresh_token` yields a ~1 h `access_token`; every entity carries a `ProfileID` (account/marketplace profile); OData conventions (`$filter`, `$expand`, `$top`, `$skip`, `@odata.nextLink`); products carry an `Attributes[] {Name, Value}` bag plus `DCQuantities`, `Labels`, `Images`; bulk via product export/upload jobs. Rebranded Rithum in 2024 (the fetched KB header reads "Welcome to Rithum API documentation").
Loses: marketplace-specific fields are encoded as **naming conventions inside a flat `Attributes` bag** with no schema, so completeness is unverifiable until the listing errors; profiles multiply everything by account×marketplace.
